data.name: Aizat
data.gender_notes: Aizat is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root 'Aza', meaning 'to help', 'to support'. This name is derived from the name of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph), who was known for his support and help towards his father and brothers. The name Aizat carries the meaning “Support, helper” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Aizat usually hope their child will grow to embody support, helper and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes support, assistance, and kindness.
data.etymology: Aizat belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Support, helper.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aizat total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Aizat ibn Jauhari was a prominent Sufi Saint and scholar from Bukhara, in present-day Uzbekistan. He is best known for establishing the Chishti order of Sufis in India. He arrived in India around 1192 CE and settled in Ajmer, where he built the famous Dargah Sharif, a mausoleum dedicated to his resting place. He died in 1205 CE.
historical_references.context: Founding Father of the Chishti Sufi Order in India

historical_references.reference: Aizat Gillani was a prominent scholar and poet from the 13th century CE in the Islamic world. Aizat is best known for his book 'Ghazaliyat', a collection of verses and commentary on the works of the famous scholar and philosopher, Al-Ghazali.
